item.title: Chip Kelly's old-school gamble, Northwestern's new-school vision have Wildcats dreaming of the College Football Playoff
item.description: EVANSTON, Ill. — Against the window seal of David Braun’s office conference room at Northwestern , a bronze statue of a man glares toward visitors. An award Braun won in 2023, the miniature depiction of Bear Bryant, dressed in his trademark suit and a houndstooth hat, is fitting considering the program’s upward trajectory and that his offense, under new coordinator Chip Kelly, is showing flashes of yesteryear: the Wing-T, Wishbone and option concepts that Bryant used to claim six national championships at Alabama more than four decades ago. “You can call them dated. That’s not fair,” Braun says with a smile. “But creative!” Life is good here in this northern Chicago suburb. The 6-1 and 18th-ranked Wildcats are off to their best start since 2012; the fall foliage sweeps across this campus like a painter’s brush; the university alignment and athletic investment is as its best since before the tumult around the clumsy handling of the end of the Pat Fitzgerald era; the program opened a more than $850 million new stadium earlier this season; and the offense is an entertaining throwback under one of the sport’s most heralded gurus. On an unseasonably warm Thursday from the school’s shimmering football facility, Kelly gnashes on breadsticks as a laminated sheet of offensive schemes protrudes from his backpocket. Two days from now he returns to Eugene for Northwestern’s game against a reeling Oregon team. He audibly shrugs. He’s returned to Oregon before, both as UCLA’s head coach and as Ohio State’s offensive coordinator in 2024. In fact, Kelly is 0-4 against the Ducks. “They’re a really good football team. They’re really talented,” he said. “Turn the tape on and you stop thinking about being nostalgic.” In his first season back in college after an 11-game stint coordinating the Raiders offense, Kelly has infused some of his old tricks into the Wildcats. He’s embracing formations, schemes and concepts that he says he hasn’t used since his days as offensive coordinator at New Hampshire — more than 20 years ago. (Adam Ruff/Getty Images) Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Upon an evaluation of the Northwestern roster during the offseason, Kelly arrived at a decision based on the talent before him: It’s time to take it old school. He dusted off his proverbial binders from his days at FCS New Hampshire: the Wing-T formation, Wishbone schemes and military academy option plays. item.title: ‘Not a tension-free zone’: Joe Buck and Troy Aikman reportedly still not happy
item.description: ESPN/ABC Monday Night Football commentators Joe Buck, left, and Troy Aikman before the Detroit Lions vs. Las Vegas Raiders game at Ford Field, Monday, Oct. 30, 2023. Joe Buck and Troy Aikman have called NFL games together for 25 seasons, and on the air, they still sound like the same old partners. But behind the scenes, things reportedly haven’t gotten much better between them. According to a new report, the friction between ESPN’s Monday Night Football duo hasn’t gone away, even after conversations with network leadership. One source said the situation is “not a tension-free zone,” and Aikman is reportedly almost certain to land somewhere else next season. Buck and Aikman’s Blowup The tension stems from the two broadcasters’ very different contract situations. Buck signed a six-year extension worth roughly $108 million that The Athletic revealed in September. Aikman, meanwhile, is in the final season of the five-year, $90 million deal he signed when the pair left Fox for ESPN in 2022. Front Office Sports’ Ryan Glasspiegel first reported the rift , revealing that Buck confronted Aikman about the friction before the Bills’ overtime win over the Rams on Oct. 12. Puck’s Dylan Byers later reported more details . According to Byers, Aikman had grown cold and curt with Buck for weeks before the confrontation and accused his partner of betraying him, since Buck’s extension had reportedly been finalized months earlier without Aikman being told. Buck later apologized to the production crew for his role in the blowup. ‘Not a Tension-Free Zone’ While Buck and Aikman have been able to keep things professional on the air, Byers reports in his latest newsletter that the friction persists, though ongoing dialogue with ESPN leadership has slightly eased the strain. “It’s not a tension-free zone,” one source told Byers, via Awful Announcing . That wasn’t obvious during Monday’s Eagles-Cowboys broadcast, which Byers called “another drama-free broadcast.” Buck got a laugh out of Aikman with a joke about Michael Irvin’s sideline celebrations, and the two did a cordial postgame hit on SportsCenter , according to The Philadelphia Inquirer . Byers credited both broadcasters’ professionalism for keeping their issues off the air. But according to his reporting, Aikman appears almost certain to be somewhere else next season. Clearly, if this is the end of the line for one of the NFL’s longest-running booths, both men are determined to finish it out without letting fans see the cracks. item.title: What needs to happen for Bengals to beat Tennessee, improve to 5-2
item.description: If you're doing a side by side comparison of the Cincinnati Bengals and Tennessee Titans , it'd be easy to assume the Nov. 1 meeting at Paycor Stadium would be a one-sided contest just based on their records. Cincinnati looks like an ascending, 4-2 team while the Titans are 1-6, and made a trade Oct. 29 that looks intended to jumpstart a rebuild effort. Four of their six losses were one-possession games ( Eagles , Giants , Ravens , Browns ) with an average margin of defeat in those contests of 4.5 points. Their lone win came against the 2-4 Indianapolis Colts . If could be exactly the kind of game where the Bengals get stuck in a nail-biter, especially considering Cincinnati is still yet to play a complete game in which the team impressed in every phase. As the calendar flips from October to November, and the Bengals enter the meat of their 2026 schedule, here's what needs to happen in order for Cincinnati to improve to 5-2 ahead of a key stretch of games: Show Cincinnati, Bengals fans, observers your true identity This is less an objective to accomplish in-game and more a plea from fans and media types seeking to pinpoint what kind of Bengals team we're looking at in 2026. Because entering Week 8, it seems fair to say many people have difficulty trying to pinpoint what we're looking at. Even the signature win - the Week 7 victory that was an embarrassment-turned-mauling against the Ravens - was, as Bengals head coach Zac Taylor conceded, a good half of football as opposed to a complete game, which it certainly wasn't. The Bengals have been carried by their defense at times (Weeks 1-3 versus Tampa Bay, Houston and Jacksonville), and eventually carried by the offense against the Ravens. The closest we've seen the team to playing complete, balanced football might have been the loss to Pittsburgh (putting aside that day's special teams major malfunctions). Bottom line, it's now Week 8. The Bengals are on the precipice of a stretch of games (at Madrid versus Atlanta followed by back-to-back primetime games on U.S. soil against Pittsburgh and Washington) that will more than likely dictate if its a legitimate contender for the AFC North title, or if it's destined for the mad scramble for a Wild Card berth. item.title: Trio of Beaver Valley runners win gold at WPIAL cross-country championships
item.description: WHITE OAK — It was a historic day for Beaver Valley high school cross country runners for a variety of ways, with individuals capturing multiple WPIAL titles, a freshman capturing her first WPIAL title, and a team putting up an unprecedented finish at the 2026 WPIAL cross country championships at White Oak Park on Thursday, Oct. 29. Two of the top boys distance runners in the state, Quaker Valley’s Jonah Montagnese and Sewickley Academy’s Zach Sharara, had gold on their minds after winning the Class 2A and 1A crowns in 2025. The pair joined rare history in the Beaver Valley, with Montagnese and Sharara becoming the sixth and seventh runners in the area’s history to win two straight WPIAL championships. “I feel super lucky to be able to come back here and blessed to win again,” Montagnese said. “It is a great achievement to have and one that I always want to have and add to the resume.” The Virginia commit finished 23 seconds ahead of the silver medalist, North Catholic’s Jack Steineman, but knew it wasn’t his best race, finishing four seconds behind the time that won him the 2A title last season. With thoughts of doubt swirling in Montagnese’s mind and Steineman trying to make a push at the defending champ, the senior pushed through. “When we hit the two-mile mark, there was a lot of doubt in my mind about this race,” Montagnese said. “I tried to work through some of the pain, take a deep breath and close hard. I was glad I was able to do that. Sharara continued his dominant run against 1A competition at this year’s championships, finishing with a time of 15:49.3. “It feels really good to go back-to-back here at WPIALs,” Sharara said. “I have been working really hard and improved a lot during the summer. Coming into the race, I didn’t care about the time that I ran; I just wanted to sit at the front, control the pace and kick it in on the final stretch.” For the beginning stages of the race, Sharara and Winchester Thurston’s Jack Iyer sat almost stride-for-stride with each other. But towards the latter half of the race, Sharara found another gear and finished just over six seconds in front to claim his second gold. “I think that I waited a little too long to push because it kind of got close towards the end,” Sharara said. “But I still think that I executed the race well was able to build a lead.” Now, after capturing another WPIAL title, Sharara has his sights set at the PIAA championships after winning bronze in Hershey last season . item.title: Max Verstappen discusses toll of F1 calendar after two drivers fall ill
item.description: Motorsport photo Four-time Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen says it is "normal" for F1 drivers and team members to fall ill at this stage of the season after two drivers missed Thursday's media day in Mexico City. Championship leader Kimi Antonelli was excused from media duties while he recovers from a viral illness, with Mercedes expecting the Italian driver to return to the track for Friday practice. Cadillac's Valtteri Bottas also missed media day through illness, with the American outfit describing it as a precaution. Mexico is the second race of a triple-header after the United States Grand Prix last week and ahead of the Brazilian Grand Prix next week. The last nine race weekends of the 2026 season are arranged into three triple-headers with one-week breaks in between them. While speaking to the media in Mexico, Verstappen was asked how tough the run of races had been. "It is, of course, always quite tough on your body, like three weeks in a row. Sometimes you can get a little bit unlucky with whatever, a stomach bug," the Dutchman explained. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, congratulates pole man Daniel Ricciardo, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, congratulates pole man Daniel Ricciardo, Red Bull Racing "But it's normally around this time of the year that not only drivers, but mechanics and people in the team get sick. Because your body can take a lot of stress. But at one point, of course, it also tells you when it needs a little recovery phase. "That's something that you need to stay on top of. And some years it goes a bit better than others. I think you try to learn about it as well a little bit with the more seasons that you do. Sometimes some things are things that you can't prevent. But for sure, it's always very tough. "For me, the toughest bit is that you can't really go home in between to be back with the family. That, for me, is nowadays something that I do not really enjoy about triple-headers." To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Vanoli frustrated by Fiorentina defending: ‘Team has talent, but must work together’

They came out fighting and turned it around through the Alieu Njie diving header and deflected Joao Mario effort, but Nicola Zalewski sealed the 2-2 result. item.title: Where Is Sidney Crosby on NHL's All-Time Points List? Penguins Star Keeps Moving Up Leaderboard
item.description: Where Is Sidney Crosby on NHL's All-Time Points List? Penguins Star Keeps Moving Up Leaderboard originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh . Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Sidney Crosby continues to climb the NHL's all-time scoring leaderboard, with another major milestone within reach as the Pittsburgh Penguins captain prepares for Thursday night's game. Crosby enters the matchup with 1,768 career points, putting him seventh in NHL history. He is just three points shy of tying Marcel Dionne for sixth place, with an opportunity to move closer to another spot among the league's all-time greats. Dionne finished his NHL career with 1,771 points across 1,348 games. Crosby has reached 1,768 points while continuing his 22nd NHL season, adding to a career that has kept him among the league's most productive players for more than two decades. Crosby would tie Dionne with three points and move into sole possession of sixth place with his fourth point. NHL All-Time Points Leaders The NHL's all-time scoring leaderboard features some of the most recognizable names in hockey history. Wayne Gretzky remains comfortably atop the list with 2,857 career points. Here is where the top 10 currently stand: Wayne Gretzky — 2,857 points Jaromir Jagr — 1,921 points Mark Messier — 1,887 points Gordie Howe — 1,850 points Ron Francis — 1,798 points Marcel Dionne — 1,771 points Sidney Crosby — 1,768 points Steve Yzerman — 1,755 points Mario Lemieux — 1,723 points Alex Ovechkin — 1,691 points Crosby has already passed several legendary players on the leaderboard, including former Penguins teammate Mario Lemieux, who finished his career with 1,723 points. The next target is Dionne, but the climb does not stop there. Ron Francis holds fifth place with 1,798 points, leaving Crosby 30 points away from reaching that mark. item.title: Max Verstappen jokes about Daniel Ricciardo's Le Mans ambition: "He's a smart man picking me!"
item.description: Motorsport photo Max Verstappen has joked that former Red Bull team-mate Daniel Ricciardo is a "smart man" for picking him in a potential trio for a future Le Mans 24 Hour challenge. Ricciardo has not taken part in any racing series since leaving F1 for the second time having raced for Red Bull's sister RB squad in 2024. However, speaking on the Beyond the Grid podcast, the Australian race winner suggested that he would be tempted to take part in a future edition of the 24-hour race around La Circuit de la Sarthe in France, highlighting Verstappen and another former Red Bull team-mate in Sebastian Vettel as a dream line-up. “I don’t want to put pressure on him, but obviously Max is a name that would be high on the list," replied Ricciardo when asked who he would choose for a partnership. Read Also: Why Daniel Ricciardo would consider a comeback at Le Mans "We talked about Red Bull obviously in 2018, and what if, and what if; I was trying to get back at the team at the end of my career, so maybe that’s a way that we could give the people what they want." Verstappen has previously mentioned a desire to one day compete at Le Mans and has dovetailed his F1 priorities with outings in GT racing, taking part in this year's Nurburgring 24 Hours and the GT World Challenge finale at Portimao. Asked ahead of this weekend's Mexico City GP about Ricciardo's comments, Verstappen replied: "He's a smart man to choose me in the car. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing "But we have to see. It just depends on a lot of things. Also for me, if I want to do it, I want to do it properly with really good prep. "At the moment I cannot do that. I don't have the free time to dedicate to a Le Mans project with all the other things that I'm also doing outside of Formula 1." Ricciardo's suggestion that Le Mans could be on the table is the first time he has revealed a desire to get back into a race car publicly, though Verstappen revealed that the news was "not new to me" having conversed with Ricciardo. "Yeah, we have spoken," confirmed the four-time world champion. "But also, I think either from my side or his side, I don't think we are the types that always need to share everything. We talk about a lot of things in the background. "I think he said it himself. He doesn't see himself coming back for a whole season but the one-offs can interest him. Why not? But again, I think if we do something like that, he will for sure agree that it needs to be proper. It needs to be for a chance to win. "For a chance to win against people that do it a whole season, you need to be prepared really well. You just need to find the right timing." To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Chancellor Lee Adams prepares for Special Olympics equestrian competition
item.description: Chancellor Lee Adams has joined a team of 12 athletes from Victory Farm in Gastonia to train for the Special Olympics equestrian competition. item.title: Max Verstappen responds to Daniel Ricciardo’s Le Mans dream team call
item.description: Motorsport photo Max Verstappen has joked that his former team-mate Daniel Ricciardo is "a smart man" for picking him for his dream Le Mans line-up. In fact, he revealed that the pair of them had already discussed the possibility of it. In a recent interview with the Beyond the Grid podcast, the Australian talked about his time at Red Bull and his exit from Formula 1. While he discussed what was next for him, he said that a Le Mans entry could be on the list. When asked who he'd team up with, Max Verstappen was the first name on his list. Sebastian Vettel was also an option, making something he called a "nice little Red Bull reunion" of sorts. “He’s a smart man to choose me in the car," Verstappen joked. "But we have to see. It just depends on a lot of things.” The four-time world champion has made no secret of his interest in endurance racing with him recently competing at Portimao, where he and his team finished ninth. He did, however, stress that he would only take on Le Mans with full preparation. “Also for me, if I want to do it, I want to do it proper with really good prep. And at the moment I cannot do that. I don’t have the time - the free time to dedicate to a Le Mans project with all the other things that I’m also doing outside of Formula 1.” Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, congratulates pole man Daniel Ricciardo, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, congratulates pole man Daniel Ricciardo, Red Bull Racing Ricciardo’s comments were the first time he had publicly spoken about racing again in any real capacity. But Verstappen said the idea had already come up between them. “This is not new to me, of course. Yeah, we have spoken,” he said. “I don’t think we are the types that always need to share everything. We talk about a lot of things in the background.” Ricciardo said a full season of racing did not appeal, and Verstappen believes that a one-off would only be worthwhile if they could be seriously competitive. “He doesn’t see himself coming back for a whole race, like a season. But the one-offs can interest him. Why not? “But again, I think if we do something like that, he will for sure agree that it needs to be proper. It needs to be for a chance to win. For a chance to win against people that do it a whole season, you need to be prepared really well. You just need to find the right timings.” Verstappen and Ricciardo were team-mates at Red Bull from 2016 to 2018. Ricciardo said on the podcast that a shared Le Mans entry could be a way to “give the people what they want” after the pair’s split at the end of 2018. item.description: 'We Got Our Swagger Back' - Angel Reese Makes Feelings Clear After Dream Force Game 7 in WNBA Finals Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese came through for her team when it mattered most, leading them to victory over the Golden State Valkyries on Thursday to force a historic Game 7 in the WNBA Finals. Reese and her Dream teammates dealt with adversity after losing a 2-1 lead, and she detailed how the team responded and saved their season with the Game 6 victory. Angel Reese Says Dream Are Confident Heading Into Game 7 of WNBA Finals Reese revealed the key to the Dream’s strong bounce-back performance while speaking to the media after the game. “I think it started with us being able to have a little players-only meeting before film and talking through things, getting our confidence, getting our swagger back,” Reese said . “You can definitely tell that we got our swagger back.” A week ago, Reese seemed to be cruising towards being named Finals MVP before the Valkyries responded to win Games 4 and 5 of the series. Reese struggled in both games and received strong criticism from fans and analysts. However, she responded in Game 6, finishing the Dream’s 80-69 win over the Valkyries with 15 points, 14 rebounds, and 6 assists. MORE: ‘Historic,’ ‘No Caitlin Clark Fan Can Slander Her Again’ – WNBA World Hypes Up Angel Reese’s Performance As Dream Force Game 7 vs. Valkyries She cited the Dream’s ability to punch first, as Atlanta won the first quarter 32-15, essentially sealing the game after 10 minutes. The Valkyries struggled defensively, as multiple Dream players hit wide-open threes. Reese helped set the tone, but her All-Star teammates also had great performances. Guard Rhyne Howard, who might be Reese’s top competition for Finals MVP if the Dream win the championship, scored 21 points and has been the team’s most consistent scoring threat during the Finals. Reese was especially proud of guard Allisha Gray, who scored 23 points and returned to form after struggling on both ends of the floor in Games 4 and 5. Gray is playing through a hand injury but appears to have her confidence back heading into Game 7. The Dream clearly played with a sense of urgency at the start of Game 6, and they’ll look to do the same in Game 7 to win the WNBA championship. Reese and her teammates are aware that the Valkyries regained some momentum in the second half of Game 6 even though they lost. The Valkyries were down by 25 points but eventually cut the deficit to single digits as they made a second-half run. As the Finals head back to the Bay Area for the WNBA season’s final chapter, Reese and her teammates are confident their swagger is back and they can finish the job. item.title: Barcelona close Camp Nou stand for Alavés clash after Eduardo Camavinga assault
item.description: Barcelona close Camp Nou stand for Alavés clash after Eduardo Camavinga assault La Liga giants Barcelona have made the call to close one of the home stands inside the Spotify Camp Nou for the club’s next La Liga outing. This comes owing to developments in last weekend’s showdown between the Blaugrana and arch rivals Real Madrid. After Kylian Mbappé netted an 88th-minute winner in Catalunya’s capital, chaos erupted in the ‘Gol 1957’ stand at the Camp Nou. Objects came raining down on top of Real Madrid’s players, whilst Eduardo Camavinga was struck by a fan with a Barcelona flag. The incident has since given rise to an official investigation, with the supporter responsible in line for a serious punishment. And as alluded to above, this week, those in a position of power at Barcelona have opted to take action of their own. As per a report from Goal , citing an official statement released by the reigning Spanish champions: ‘Barcelona have decided to suspend the activity of the Gol 1957 stand, known as the supporters’ stand, during the upcoming league match against Alavés. ‘This decision comes in response to a series of disciplinary proceedings opened against the club and some of its members, on the back of behaviour that runs contrary to sporting values. These actions expose the club to financial penalties, to the risk of the stadium being closed, as well as damaging its image. ‘The club will meet with representatives of the groups that make up the Gol 1957 stand to discuss the situation and determine the commitments necessary to maintain passionate and respectful support that contributes to backing the team without putting Barcelona’s property or reputation at risk. ‘The club’s wish is for the Gol 1957 stand to return to operating at full capacity during the Aston Villa match, provided that these discussions allow the situation to be rectified and ensure the proper running of things. ‘Support is an important element the club wishes to preserve, stemming from the shared commitment and responsibility of everyone, for the benefit of Barcelona.’ Conor Laird – GSFN

item.description: Photo: City of Detroit / Wikimedia Commons (Public Domain) Sting Ray Robb’s move to United Autosports for the 2026/27 Asian Le Mans Series will be packaged as an IndyCar driver trying sports cars. That undersells it. The more useful read is that Robb has signed up for an exam in a skill IndyCar almost never tests: going fast through a crowd of slower cars, then handing a hot seat to two other drivers. The confirmed part is simple. United announced on October 28 that Robb, 25, will drive its No. 22 ORECA 07 LMP2 car alongside Ian Aguilera and Giorgio Roda. The season is six four-hour races across three European double-headers: Paul Ricard on November 13–15, Jerez on January 15–17 and Portimão on February 19–21. The series says it moved the whole calendar to Europe temporarily, away from the Middle East. The traffic is the exam Here is the number that matters. The series capped its full-season grid at 47 entries: two Ferrari 499P Hypercars, 16 LMP2 cars and 29 GT3 cars. Robb’s ORECA will spend most of every stint catching cars from a slower class, since GT3 machines are roughly six in ten of the field. That is my read of why this is harder than it looks. In a single-class series, every car ahead is a rival, and passing is a fight. In LMP2, most of the cars you catch are not rivals at all. The job is to get by cleanly without losing a second to the move or costing someone else their race. It is judgment more than outright speed, and it is the one thing a single-seater résumé can’t show. United Autosports’ No. 22 ORECA 07 at Watkins Glen in 2025, the same model and car number Robb will share in Europe. Photo: SmackJam / Wikimedia Commons ( CC BY-SA 4.0 ) A résumé that explains the appeal IndyCar’s own driver page lists Robb with 69 career starts and no wins or top-five finishes. He finished 2026 25th in points in the No. 77 Juncos Hollinger Chevrolet, in a season that ended with the finale at Laguna Seca . There are bright spots: United points to the 23 laps he led at the 2024 Indianapolis 500. So the attraction is easy to see. United is the 2026 European Le Mans Series champion, which makes this a car that is expected to win. Robb himself framed it that way, saying the goal is “to fight at the front and win races.” For a driver whose IndyCar results have rarely matched his seat time, a front-running ride is the rarest thing on offer. United’s announcement says nothing about his 2027 IndyCar plans, and this is not a comment on them. The teammates set the bar Robb is not walking into an empty car. Roda took five poles from six qualifying sessions with United last winter, according to the team, and Aguilera, 19, finished fifth in LMP2 on his Le Mans debut in 2026. In a three-driver crew the slowest stint is everyone’s problem, so Robb will be measured against a proven one-lap qualifier and a teenager with a Le Mans class result. item.title: Giants Emerge as Potential Trade Suitor for Future Hall of Famer
item.description: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - OCTOBER 11: Head coach John Harbaugh of the New York Giants looks on during the fourth quarter of the game against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) Getty The New York Giants, sitting alone atop the NFC East at 4-2-1, have been named as a potential trade suitor to watch for Los Angeles Chargers edge rusher Khalil Mack. FanSided’s Michael Haney was the one who suggested Mack as a potential target to watch. With the Chargers remaining the NFL’s only winless team at 0-6, general manager Joe Schoen could find a low-cost opportunity to address a thinned-out edge room. The Giants have positioned themselves as buyers at the Nov. 10 trade deadline after a strong start under first-year head coach John Harbaugh. Their defense, coordinated by Dennard Wilson, has shown promise but carries clear vulnerabilities on the perimeter. Edge Room Needs Reinforcement Brian Burns, the team’s highest-paid defender, suffered a season-ending ACL tear early in the year, removing the unit’s most proven pass-rush presence. Kayvon Thibodeaux has logged a heavy snap share in Burns’ absence yet has recorded zero sacks through roughly six games while playing on a fifth-year option worth more than $14 million. Thibodeaux has contributed in the run game at times, but his pass-rush production has lagged, making him a possible trade candidate himself. Rookie Abdul Carter has stepped up with strong pressure rates and high marks from Pro Football Focus, yet the Giants remain limited when facing physical run schemes. Haney noted that without Burns, the edge group lacks the consistent edge-setting needed for Wilson’s aggressive scheme. Mack, a 13-year veteran, would represent an immediate upgrade over Thibodeaux in that specific area. Veteran Presence Could Stabilize Front Mack has recorded three sacks and 19 total tackles in six games this season for the Chargers while ranking among the league’s more reliable run defenders at the position. He entered 2026 with 116 career sacks and a long track record of setting the edge, a trait that distinguishes him from pure speed rushers such as Carter and Burns. Haney wrote that Mack is stronger against the run than either of those players and would strengthen the Giants’ ability to contain outside runs. The analysis suggests Schoen should pursue the deal if the cost is only a fourth-round pick, preserving future draft capital while adding a proven veteran. Mack is playing on a one-year contract, limiting long-term salary commitments for a contending Giants team. Adding him would allow the coaching staff to rotate Thibodeaux or move him if a favorable offer arrives. The Giants’ defensive front has been among the more productive units in the league when healthy, but depth has become a clear concern after Burns’ injury and other attrition. A short-term addition like Mack could help maintain momentum as New York aims for a division title

Arizona Diamondbacks right-hander Corbin Burnes will remain with the club after deciding against opting out of his contract , committing to four more seasons worth $140 million through 2030, USA Today’s Bob Nightengale reported on Thursday. The former National League Cy Young Award winner will collect $35 million annually from 2027 through 2030, although $11 million per season will be deferred. Burnes signed a six-year, $210 million contract with Arizona in December 2024, making it the largest deal in franchise history at the time, surpassing Zack Greinke’s $206.5 million agreement from 2015. However, injuries have considerably limited his contributions during the first two years of the partnership. The 2021 NL Cy Young Award winner made 11 starts in 2025 before undergoing Tommy John surgery in June after suffering a torn ulnar collateral ligament. His recovery extended into the following season, with a teres major strain in June delaying his anticipated return. Although Burnes eventually came off the injured list in September 2026, he managed only three starts before shoulder inflammation sidelined him again. Burnes surrendered nine earned runs across 10.1 innings, recording a 7.84 ERA while allowing five home runs. His velocity and command were inconsistent, and he was unable to effectively utilize his cutter. In his final outing, he gave up three home runs in 2.2 innings. Nevertheless, the Diamondbacks remain hopeful that a full offseason will help Burnes recover his previous form. The shoulder inflammation is not expected to become a long-term issue, although his workload could be restricted after missing most of the past two seasons. Burnes own a career 3.20 ERA across 213 appearances, including a 2.86 ERA from 2020 through 2025. He will turn 32 before the 2027 season begins. His decision also leaves Arizona responsible for the remaining financial commitment, even as the organization is expected to reduce its payroll to some extent next season. Burnes reportedly turned down larger offers from other teams when signing with the Diamondbacks, with his family’s home in Scottsdale among the considerations behind that decision. With Burnes expected back in the rotation, Arizona can pair him with Eduardo Rodriguez, Merrill Kelly, Brandon Pfaadt and Ryne Nelson. Arizona could also explore bringing back Michael Soroka, who has a $10 million mutual option, or add another pitcher to bolster the starting staff. The Diamondbacks will now need their record-setting investment to prove its worth through consistent production, with Burnes’ health and effectiveness central to the rotation’s outlook for 2027 and beyond.
